slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Volume of a pyramid or cone: V = (1/3)Bh.

A cube can be cut into three congruent pyramids, each with a face of the cube as its base and the opposite corner as its apex. Each has volume one third of the cube's. By Cavalieri's Principle, any two pyramids with equal base areas and heights have equal volume, because their cross sections at the same height are scaled copies of the bases by the same factor.

A cone filled with rice three times fills a cylinder of the same base and height. A cone is a third of a cylinder, not half.
